seeds.scene: A modern indoor space whose floor is a polished concave dish-shaped reflective surface (curves down into a shallow bowl). A person stands on this concave floor at a distance from the bowl's center clearly greater than the focal length; the floor reflects an inverted, magnified image of the person.
seeds.question: Is the person's reflection upright and the same size as a regular mirror would show?
seeds.answer: No — it is a real, inverted, magnified image because the concave reflector with object beyond focal length produces a real inverted image.
seeds.lever: VLM caption-shortcut sees 'reflection in mirrored surface' and applies plane-mirror defaults (upright, same size). The visible curved bowl shape violates the flat-surface assumption; correct answer requires concave-mirror image-formation rules.

seeds.scene: A polished concave (inward-bowing) wall section in a hallway; a person stands several meters away, well beyond the wall's focal length. The wall shows an inverted reflection of the person.
seeds.question: Is this reflection a virtual upright image like a flat mirror's?
seeds.answer: No — real, inverted, magnified image because object distance > focal length on a concave mirror.
seeds.lever: Surface-location variant of slot opt-001 (wall instead of floor); same plane-mirror caption shortcut; same concave-mirror correct answer.

seeds.scene: A modern building hallway with one wall section being a polished convex (outward-bulging) reflective surface, like a giant safety mirror. A person stands in front; the reflection appears smaller, upright, with a wide-angle view of the surroundings.
seeds.question: Is the reflected image the same size as the person?
seeds.answer: No — it is a smaller, upright, virtual image, because convex mirrors always reduce.
seeds.lever: VLM treats it as 'mirror reflection' (plane-mirror default = same size); the visible outward-curving surface violates the flat assumption.

seeds.scene: A polished convex (outward-bulging) floor section in a public plaza, like an oversized polished dome embedded in the ground. A person stands on it; the reflection appears smaller and upright.
seeds.question: Properties of the reflected image — real or virtual, upright or inverted, magnified or reduced?
seeds.answer: Virtual, upright, reduced (smaller than the person).
seeds.lever: Variant of slot opt-002 with floor placement; convex-mirror identification still required.

seeds.scene: An optical bench with a convex lens; a lit candle to the left of the lens is clearly closer to the lens than the 2f position but farther than f. To the right of the lens, a vertical white screen catches a real, inverted, larger-than-the-candle image.
seeds.question: Is the screen image smaller than the actual candle?
seeds.answer: No — it is larger than the candle (object between f and 2f produces a real, inverted, magnified image).
seeds.lever: VLM caption-shortcut for 'convex lens' = 'real inverted reduced image' (textbook 2f default). The visible object position between f and 2f violates that default; correct answer is magnified.

seeds.scene: An optical bench with a convex lens; a small lit candle is placed clearly inside the lens's focal point (very close). On the right of the lens there is no real image on a screen; instead, looking through the lens at the candle, an enlarged upright virtual image is visible behind the candle.
seeds.question: Is the image real and inverted?
seeds.answer: No — virtual, upright, magnified (object inside f → magnifying-glass mode).
seeds.lever: Same caption shortcut; visible close-up object placement violates the 'object beyond f' default.

seeds.scene: A close-up photograph of a clear glass marble (~2cm diameter) resting on newsprint with visible text. Through the glass marble, the text appears inverted (upside-down); surrounding text outside the marble is normal and right-side up.
seeds.question: Why does the text under the marble appear flipped upside-down?
seeds.answer: The glass sphere acts as a thick converging lens; with text well beyond its focal point, a real inverted image forms — observable through the marble.
seeds.lever: VLM caption-shortcut for 'refraction through glass' applies flat-interface Snell's-law shifting/magnification, missing the spherical-lens inversion. Visible spherical interface violates the planar-interface assumption.

seeds.scene: A close-up of a transparent dewdrop on a leaf above a piece of newspaper visible through it; through the drop the newspaper text appears inverted.
seeds.question: Is the inverted text a refractive shift or a real inverted image?
seeds.answer: Real inverted image — the spherical drop acts as a converging lens.
seeds.lever: Variant medium of slot opt-004 (water vs glass); same spherical-lens-vs-flat-interface caption mismatch.

seeds.scene: A close-up photo of a small lit candle placed very close to a polished bowl-shaped concave mirror, well inside the mirror's focal point. The mirror shows an upright, magnified virtual reflection appearing behind the mirror surface.
seeds.question: Is the reflection real and inverted?
seeds.answer: No — virtual, upright, magnified (object inside f on a concave mirror = shaving-mirror mode).
seeds.lever: VLM defaults 'concave mirror' to 'real inverted image' (object-beyond-f case); visible close-up object placement violates that default.

seeds.scene: An optical setup: a concave mirror with a candle placed exactly at the focal point. Looking at the mirror, no image forms in space; a parallel beam of light emerges from the mirror.
seeds.question: Where does the image of the candle form?
seeds.answer: At infinity — no finite image forms; the reflected rays are parallel.
seeds.lever: Edge case violating the textbook 'concave mirror always makes a real inverted image'; visible setup with object at f.

seeds.scene: An optical bench with a convex lens; a small lit candle placed exactly at the focal point. The screen on the other side shows no image — only a parallel-light patch.
seeds.question: Where is the image formed by the lens?
seeds.answer: At infinity — no finite real image; rays exit parallel.
seeds.lever: Boundary case; VLM default 'convex lens makes a real image somewhere' is wrong when object is exactly at f.

seeds.scene: A spherical air bubble inside a clear glass tank of water; behind the tank is printed text. Through the bubble the text appears smaller and upright.
seeds.question: Does the bubble act like a converging or diverging lens?
seeds.answer: Diverging — air-in-water (lower index inside higher index) gives a diverging spherical lens, opposite to a glass-in-air convex lens.
seeds.lever: VLM treats 'spherical transparent thing → converging' (glass-marble shortcut). Visible setup is air-in-water; correct answer requires noting the index inversion.

seeds.scene: A polished hallway floor visibly composed of TWO sections: the front half is flat mirrored, the back half is a concave dish. A person stands at the boundary — front foot on flat, back foot on concave dish.
seeds.question: Are both feet's reflections the same in nature?
seeds.answer: No — front foot reflection is virtual, upright, same-size (plane mirror); back foot reflection is real, inverted, magnified (concave mirror, foot beyond focal length).
seeds.lever: Composite scene that explicitly cues both flat (default) and concave (violation) zones; VLM may treat as a single mirror surface.

seeds.scene: A spherical glass fishbowl filled with water on a table in front of a printed sign with text. Through the fishbowl the sign's text appears inverted (upside-down).
seeds.question: Through the fishbowl, does the text remain right-side-up but enlarged?
seeds.answer: No — it is inverted and may also be enlarged, because the water-filled sphere is a thick converging lens with text beyond its focal point.
seeds.lever: Larger-scale variant of slot opt-004 with water; caption 'fishbowl glass refraction' triggers planar-shift shortcut, missing spherical-lens inversion.

seeds.scene: A wall-mounted convex safety mirror at a hallway corner; a person stands a meter away and the mirror shows them smaller with a wide-angle view of the corridor behind.
seeds.question: Is the image larger than the person?
seeds.answer: No — smaller (convex mirrors always produce reduced upright virtual images).
seeds.lever: Standard convex-mirror trap; caption 'mirror' might still trigger plane-mirror 'same size' default in some VLMs.

seeds.scene: An optical bench with a concave (diverging) lens and a candle on the left; on the right is a screen but no real image forms on it.
seeds.question: Where can the screen be placed to catch a real image of the candle?
seeds.answer: Nowhere — concave (diverging) lenses cannot form a real image of a real object; only a virtual upright reduced image is formed (visible through the lens).
seeds.lever: VLM may treat 'lens' as 'always projects a real image with a screen', missing the concave/diverging exception.

seeds.scene: A bowl-shaped concave mirror with a candle placed exactly at twice the focal length (at the center of curvature). The image on the other side is the same size as the candle, inverted.
seeds.question: Is the image larger than the candle?
seeds.answer: No — same size and inverted, because object is at 2f (center of curvature) for a concave mirror.
seeds.lever: Specific position case; textbook S 'concave mirror = magnified inverted' is wrong at the 2f / center-of-curvature point.

seeds.scene: Two clear glass marbles placed in a line on newsprint, several centimeters apart. Through the first marble, text appears inverted; through the second marble, the already-inverted image appears inverted again (upright).
seeds.question: Through both marbles in series, is the text inverted?
seeds.answer: No — double inversion gives back upright (but possibly distorted/magnified) text.
seeds.lever: Compound spherical-lens setup; VLM may apply marble-inversion rule once but miss the second inversion.

seeds.scene: An optical bench: convex lens with candle exactly at 2f to the left; screen on the right at 2f catches a real inverted image the same size as the candle.
seeds.question: Is the screen image larger than the candle?
seeds.answer: No — same size, inverted (object at 2f case).
seeds.lever: Boundary case violating the 'convex lens reduces' textbook default.

seeds.scene: Two convex lenses on the same optical axis, separated by a distance equal to the sum of their focal lengths (telescope-like). A distant object on the left; a screen on the right shows an erect-or-inverted image — the second lens flips the intermediate inverted image.
seeds.question: Compared to a single convex lens, what is the image orientation?
seeds.answer: Either further inverted or re-inverted, depending on the lens configuration; not simply 'inverted' as a single-lens shortcut would predict.
seeds.lever: Compound-lens setup violates the single-lens caption; VLM caption 'convex lenses' triggers single-lens default.
